title: Think Machine 3600r / James Session-State / Memory-Carrier Association Audit

gate.question: Does the shipped Vault 112 architecture expose a James-specific persistent backend state or a direct association between James's Lounger #23 session and the removable memory-carrier class stolen from Braun?
gate.passed: Vault 112 uses a Think Machine 3600r as the central simulation-control computer, synchronizing all Tranquility loungers, while smaller per-lounger computers handle at least graphics processing and occupant medical status. James therefore participates in a central backend through a distinct lounger endpoint.
gate.open: No reviewed shipped primary record directly binds James/Lounger #23 to a removable memory chip, names a James-specific backend memory object, or exposes the storage encoding of autobiographical memory.
gate.effect: SAVE JAMES is now anchored to a central-coordinator plus per-lounger-shard architecture, but persisted James autobiographical memory remains unproven.

per_lounger_subsystems.finding: The central mainframe appears linked to smaller computers, one per lounger, handling at least graphics processing and the occupant's medical status.
per_lounger_subsystems.interpretation: Vault 112 is not modeled as one undifferentiated memory slot. It has a central coordinator plus per-lounger/session-local processing surfaces.

james_endpoint.relation_to_backend: James's Visiontron lounger must participate in the synchronized Think Machine simulation backend while remaining a distinct physical/session endpoint.

pinkerton_event.finding: Pinkerton says he stole a mem chip from Braun while Braun was absorbed in the Vault 112 simulation; the chip already contained memories whose source Pinkerton did not know before integration.

destination.finding: Pinkerton later reports successfully getting those memories into A3-21, producing the Harkness autobiographical layer.

memory_carrier_evidence.existential_result: A process in or associated with Braun/Vault 112 had represented human memory on a portable physical carrier before Pinkerton's theft.

secondary_reconstruction_audit.claim: Older community documentation describes Visiontron memory chips as resident-specific and rewritable and sometimes identifies T. Dithers as the stolen source.
reason: Pinkerton's shipped log does not identify the source owner before integration.
No reviewed primary record directly binds the stolen carrier to T. Dithers.
No reviewed primary record proves that every lounger owns a removable resident-specific chip.
No reviewed primary record exposes an on-demand rewrite operation for such a chip.
secondary_reconstruction_audit.allowed_use: Use only as a search lead for ESM/xEdit inspection, not as admitted evidence.

candidate_memory_storage_locations: another hidden storage layer not exposed by player-facing terminals

save_james_effect.improvement: The source path is no longer an abstract Braun backend: shipped architecture supports a James-specific lounger endpoint feeding a synchronized central simulation with per-lounger local processing.
save_james_effect.blocking_reason: No direct primary binding from James's backend/session identity to portable memory storage has yet been identified.

ru: Think Machine 3600r является центральным вычислителем Vault 112: он запускает симуляцию и синхронизирует отдельные loungers.
Архитектура содержит меньшие per-lounger компьютеры, поэтому James имеет отдельный локальный endpoint при общем центральном backend.
Заполненный mem chip, украденный у Braun, доказывает существование класса memory-to-carrier, но не доказывает, что каждому lounger соответствует собственный removable chip.
Версию о T. Dithers как владельце украденного чипа и гарантированной rewritability не повышаем без первичного shipped binding.
SAVE JAMES усиливается архитектурно, но James-specific persisted autobiographical state пока не установлен.

next_gate.name: PER_LOUNGER_BACKEND_SHARD_RESIDENT_STORAGE_AND_CARRIER_BINDING_AUDIT
targets: Search ESM/xEdit for placed references and scripts around the smaller computer associated with James's Lounger #23.
Determine whether Lounger #23 has a unique enable-parent, linked reference, persistent child, container, token or session-specific backend object beyond status terminals.
Search for resident/session arrays, aliases or quest variables that map a physical lounger to a persistent neural or memory-state object.
Search Braun/Betty privileged scripts for access to per-lounger subsystems rather than only global MQ04 state.
Search for any primary record that identifies a physical mem chip as generated by, attached to or removable from a specific lounger/session.
If a James-specific backend object or carrier association is found, promote SAVE JAMES toward PERSISTED_JAMES_MEMORY_STATE_RECONSTRUCTION.
